canonical_statement: Nothing in existence truly perishes; what is perceived as death or destruction is merely a change in state.

attributions.surface_quote: No one of existing things doth perish, but men in error speak of their changes.

canonical_statement: The divine is inherently manifest despite being unmanifest to the senses.

attributions.surface_quote: Though Unmanifest God Is Most Manifest.

canonical_statement: The highest form of human suffering arises from a lack of knowledge regarding the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: The Greatest Ill Among Men is Ignorance of God.

canonical_statement: The individual mind can transcend sensory perception to access higher states of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: my thought was raised to a great height, the senses of my body being held back

canonical_statement: A universal, omniscient intelligence exists that is omnipresent and accessible to the individual.

attributions.surface_quote: I am Man-Shepherd, Mind of all-masterhood; I know what thou desirest and I'm with thee everywhere.

canonical_statement: The ultimate nature of reality is a limitless, unified Light.

attributions.surface_quote: I see a Vision limitless, all things turned into Light.

canonical_statement: The Divine Mind exists prior to and independent of the material, moist nature.

attributions.surface_quote: Mind, prior to Moist Nature which appeared from Darkness.

canonical_statement: The Logos (Word) and the Mind are inseparable, and their union constitutes the essence of Life.

attributions.surface_quote: Not separate are they the one from other; just in their union is it Life consists.

canonical_statement: Individual human perception and cognition are manifestations of the Divine Logos.

attributions.surface_quote: What sees in thee and hears is the Lord's Word.

canonical_statement: The material universe is animated and ordered by the pervading influence of the Spirit-Word.

attributions.surface_quote: Earth-and-Water stayed so mingled... moved to hear by reason of the Spirit-Word.

canonical_statement: The totality of existence is a singular, unified consciousness that encompasses all things.

attributions.surface_quote: All is one and one is all.

canonical_statement: The material world is a reflection or manifestation of a divine, non-material intellect.

attributions.surface_quote: The world is an image of the divine mind.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness possesses the inherent capacity to recognize its own divine origin.

attributions.surface_quote: Man can know his own divine nature.

canonical_statement: The soul is an immortal entity distinct from the transient physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: The soul is immortal and the body is mortal.

canonical_statement: The archetypal form of reality exists prior to time and is eternal.

attributions.surface_quote: Archetypal Form whose being is before beginning without end.

canonical_statement: The physical cosmos is a derivative copy of the divine archetypal form, manifested through the Will of God.

attributions.surface_quote: Nature received the Word, and gazing upon the Cosmos Beautiful did copy it.

canonical_statement: The divine substrate is inherently dual-gendered, existing as both Light and Life.

attributions.surface_quote: God-the-Mind, being male and female both, as Light and Life subsisting.

canonical_statement: Matter becomes distinct from spirit when the divine Logos withdraws from the lower elements.

attributions.surface_quote: Nature's downward elements were thus left reason-less, so as to be pure matter.

canonical_statement: Humanity is a direct, co-equal image of the Divine Mind, endowed with the capacity for creative formation.

attributions.surface_quote: All-Father Mind did bring forth Man co-equal to Himself, the Image of his Sire.

canonical_statement: The incarnation of consciousness into the material realm occurs through the projection of the divine image into nature.

attributions.surface_quote: He vivified the form devoid of reason.

canonical_statement: The universe is a unified, living entity permeated by a singular divine intelligence.

attributions.surface_quote: The universe is a living entity permeated by divine intelligence.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness is a reflection of the divine mind, capable of recognizing its own source.

attributions.surface_quote: Human consciousness is a reflection of the divine mind.

canonical_statement: Material reality is an illusion or shadow cast by the higher, immutable realm of forms.

attributions.surface_quote: Material reality is a shadow of the higher realm.

canonical_statement: Human identity is dualistic, consisting of a mortal physical body and an immortal essential self.

attributions.surface_quote: man is twofold; mortal because of body, but because of the essential man immortal.

canonical_statement: The immortal human essence is subject to the constraints of Fate and the Harmony of the spheres while embodied.

attributions.surface_quote: Though deathless... yet doth he suffer as a mortal doth, subject to Fate.

canonical_statement: The material world is composed of seven distinct natures derived from Fire and Spirit.

attributions.surface_quote: seven 'men', in correspondence with the natures of the Seven, made of Fire and Spirit.

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness (Mind) and soul are derived from the primordial principles of Light and Life.

attributions.surface_quote: Man from Light and Life changed into soul and mind.

canonical_statement: Attachment to the physical body through desire is the fundamental cause of mortality and suffering.

attributions.surface_quote: the cause of death is love... he who expends his love upon his body stays in Darkness.

canonical_statement: Self-knowledge of one's immortal nature is the mechanism for transcending the cycle of death.

attributions.surface_quote: he who thus hath learned to know himself, hath reached that Good which doth transcend.

canonical_statement: The universe is a singular, unified entity encompassing all existence.

attributions.surface_quote: The All is one and the one is the All.

canonical_statement: The human mind is a reflection or fragment of the divine intellect.

attributions.surface_quote: Mind is the child of God.

canonical_statement: Physical reality is a manifestation of divine thought and will.

attributions.surface_quote: The world is the image of God.

canonical_statement: Knowledge of the self is equivalent to knowledge of the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: Know thyself to know the Divine.

canonical_statement: The material world is rooted in darkness, which serves as the foundation for the physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: the gloomy Darkness is the root and base of the material frame

canonical_statement: Human identity is fundamentally derived from the divine principles of Light and Life.

attributions.surface_quote: the Father of the universals doth consist of Light and Life, from Him Man was born

canonical_statement: Deathlessness is achieved by recognizing one's essential nature as being composed of Light and Life.

attributions.surface_quote: learn that thou art thyself of Life and Light... thou shalt return again to Life

canonical_statement: The divine Mind is not universally present in all humans, but manifests specifically in those who are pure and pious.

attributions.surface_quote: I, Mind, myself am present with holy men and good

canonical_statement: The divine Mind acts as a filter, preventing base sensory operations from influencing the consciousness of the pious.

attributions.surface_quote: I, the Mind, that will not let the operations which befall the body, work

canonical_statement: The absence of the divine Mind results in the soul being subjected to an Avenging Daimon that amplifies sensory desire and suffering.

attributions.surface_quote: to the Mind-less ones... I am far off, yielding my place to the Avenging Daimon

canonical_statement: At death, the physical form dissolves, and the sensory faculties return to their original elemental sources as energies.

attributions.surface_quote: The body's senses next pass back into their sources, becoming separate, and resurrect as energies

canonical_statement: The soul ascends through planetary spheres, shedding specific worldly vices and attachments at each stage.

attributions.surface_quote: man doth speed his way thereafter upwards through the Harmony... de-energized

canonical_statement: The ultimate state of the soul is the dissolution of individual identity into the Divine.

attributions.surface_quote: becoming Powers they are in God... to be made one with God

canonical_statement: Humanity possesses an inherent, latent capacity for immortality that is obscured by ignorance.

attributions.surface_quote: why have ye given yourselves up to Death, while yet ye have the power of sharing Deathlessness?

canonical_statement: Physical sensory experience and bodily states are inversely related to spiritual perception and awakening.

attributions.surface_quote: body's sleep became the soul's awakening, and closing of the eyes - true vision

canonical_statement: The Divine Will realizes itself through its own inherent powers.

attributions.surface_quote: God, whose Will perfects itself by means of its own Powers.

canonical_statement: The Logos is the instrument through which the universe is brought into existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou who didst by Word (Logos) make to consist the things that are.

canonical_statement: The natural world is an image of the Divine.

attributions.surface_quote: Holy art Thou, of whom All-nature hath been made an image.

canonical_statement: Gnosis is the fundamental nature of human existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Gnosis, which is our common being's nature.

canonical_statement: All motion requires a container that is greater than the object moved.

attributions.surface_quote: Must not that in which it's moved be greater than the moved?

canonical_statement: The mover must possess a different nature and greater power than the object moved.

attributions.surface_quote: Mover, again, has greater power than moved?

canonical_statement: Space is a bodiless entity that exists independently of physical matter.

attributions.surface_quote: Space, then, is bodiless.

canonical_statement: God transcends substance and is defined as the energy that contains all space.

attributions.surface_quote: God... as energy that can contain all space.

canonical_statement: God is only 'thinkable' to human consciousness because He is an object of perception, not because He is inherently thinkable to Himself.

attributions.surface_quote: God is first 'thinkable' for us, not for Himself.

canonical_statement: Motion requires a stable, stationary substrate; nothing can move within that which is itself moving.

attributions.surface_quote: All that is moved is moved not in the moved but in the stable.

canonical_statement: The appearance of movement in physical systems is the result of resistance between opposing forces, which manifests as a form of rest.

attributions.surface_quote: Resistance is the rest of motion.

canonical_statement: Stability is achieved through the interaction of contrary motions.

attributions.surface_quote: The contrary stands firm, being rendered ever stable by its contrariety.

canonical_statement: All motion is generated by internal incorporeal principles rather than external physical forces.

attributions.surface_quote: All motion is caused in station and by station... by things interior.

canonical_statement: Only animate entities possess the capacity to act as movers of physical matter.

attributions.surface_quote: That which doth move another thing is animate, in that it is the mover.

canonical_statement: Absolute void or emptiness does not exist within the nature of reality.

attributions.surface_quote: Naught of things that are is void. Alone the is-not is void.

canonical_statement: The universe contains no true void, as all space is permeated by air and spirit.

attributions.surface_quote: These, then, which thou dost say are void... are full of air and spirit.

canonical_statement: The space in which all things move is the 'Bodiless,' defined as Mind and Reason.

attributions.surface_quote: What are we, then, to call that space in which the all doth move? The bodiless.

canonical_statement: Existence is composed entirely of things that are; non-existence has no power to be.

attributions.surface_quote: they are all from things-that-are and not from things-that-are-not.

canonical_statement: God is not an entity or attribute, but the primary Cause of all attributes such as Mind, Spirit, and Light.

attributions.surface_quote: God, therefore, is not Mind, but Cause that the Mind is.

canonical_statement: The Good is the sole essence of God and is distinct from the nature of soul and body.

attributions.surface_quote: He is Good alone and nothing else. The rest of things are separable all from the Good's nature.

canonical_statement: The nature of the Divine is identical to the nature of the Good.

attributions.surface_quote: God's nature and the Good is one.

canonical_statement: The Divine is the absolute source of all things, characterized by pure giving without reception.

attributions.surface_quote: The Good is he who gives all things and naught receives.

canonical_statement: The Divine functions as the Father through the act of creation.

attributions.surface_quote: The other name of God is Father, because He is that-which-maketh-all.

canonical_statement: Procreation is a metaphysical duty, and failure to reproduce results in post-mortem karmic retribution.

attributions.surface_quote: He who hath no child is punished by the daimones after death.

canonical_statement: The soul's post-mortem state is determined by the fulfillment of earthly biological obligations.

attributions.surface_quote: That man's soul who hath no child, shall be condemned unto a body with neither man's nor woman's nature.

canonical_statement: The Divine is the fundamental substrate of all existence, encompassing Mind, Nature, Matter, and the cyclical process of renewal.

attributions.surface_quote: Source of the things that are is God, who is both Mind and Nature.

canonical_statement: The material universe emerged from a primordial state of chaos through the imposition of Divine Light and the separation of elements.

attributions.surface_quote: Then Holy Light arose; and there collected 'neath Dry Space from out Moist Essence Elements.

canonical_statement: The structure of the cosmos is organized into hierarchical layers based on the density of elements, sustained by Divine Breath.

attributions.surface_quote: the light things were assigned unto the height, the heavy ones had their foundations laid down.

canonical_statement: All biological life forms contain an inherent, self-replicating capacity for regeneration and reproduction.

attributions.surface_quote: everything that beareth seed... all having in themselves seed of again-becoming.

canonical_statement: The celestial bodies and the natural order are governed by divine entities who act as agents of the Divine Will.

attributions.surface_quote: every God by his own proper power brought forth what was appointed him.

canonical_statement: Human incarnation is orchestrated by celestial cycles to facilitate the observation and understanding of divine energy and natural law.

attributions.surface_quote: every soul infleshed by revolution of the Cyclic Gods, for observation of the marvels

canonical_statement: All physical forms and human creations are subject to a perpetual cycle of decay and renewal governed by divine and natural rhythms.

attributions.surface_quote: every birth of flesh ensouled... shall of necessity renew itself

canonical_statement: Nature is ontologically co-established within the Godhead, functioning as the mechanism of divine renewal.

attributions.surface_quote: Nature herself is also co-established in that Godhead

canonical_statement: The universe is a manifestation of the Creator's Will and Reason, existing as an intangible, non-material substrate.

attributions.surface_quote: With Reason, not with hands, did the World-maker make the universal World.

canonical_statement: Humanity possesses a dual nature, being simultaneously mortal and immortal.

attributions.surface_quote: man, a life that cannot die, and yet a life that dies.

canonical_statement: The faculty of Mind is not innate to all humans but is an external prize to be attained through conscious effort.

attributions.surface_quote: He willed, my son, to have it set up in the midst for souls, just as it were a prize.

canonical_statement: The realization of one's origin and the capacity for faith are prerequisites for the attainment of higher consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: thou that hast faith thou canst ascend to him that hath sent down the Cup.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness is bifurcated into the faculty of Reason and the faculty of Mind, the latter being the prerequisite for Gnosis.

attributions.surface_quote: they who do not understand... possess the aid of Reason [only] and not Mind

canonical_statement: Reality is dualistic, consisting of the Body (perishing) and the Bodiless (divine), which cannot coexist within the same consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: existing things are twain, Body and Bodiless... it can never be the twain should meet

canonical_statement: The soul's liberation from the body is a matter of individual choice, and the growth of one state necessitates the waning of the other.

attributions.surface_quote: the waning of the one causes the other's growth to show itself

canonical_statement: The Divine (the Good) is infinite, without beginning or end, and exists beyond the reach of human temporal perception.

attributions.surface_quote: to the Good there is no other shore; It hath no bounds

canonical_statement: Evil is not a product of the Divine, but arises from human preference and choice.

attributions.surface_quote: 'tis not God, 'tis we who are the cause of evil things

canonical_statement: The soul must traverse a complex system of celestial bodies and daimonic choirs to return to the One.

attributions.surface_quote: how many are the bodies through which we have to pass... to hasten to the One

canonical_statement: The ultimate Good is incorporeal and therefore imperceptible to physical senses.

attributions.surface_quote: the Good can never show Itself unto the eyes, for It hath neither form

canonical_statement: The Oneness is the self-originated source of all existence and is not dependent on any external cause.

attributions.surface_quote: The Oneness being Source and Root of all, is in all things as Root

canonical_statement: The Oneness contains all multiplicity while remaining indivisible and uncontained by any other entity.

attributions.surface_quote: The Oneness then being Source, containeth every number, but is contained by none

canonical_statement: All engendered things are inherently imperfect and divisible, subject to growth and decay.

attributions.surface_quote: all that is engendered is imperfect, it is divisible, to increase subject and to decrease

canonical_statement: Divine perception acts as an attractive force that draws the observer toward the source.

attributions.surface_quote: the Sight [Divine] hath this peculiar [charm], it holdeth fast and draweth unto it

canonical_statement: The ultimate divine reality is inherently unmanifest and exists beyond the process of becoming.

attributions.surface_quote: The Unmanifest for ever is, for It doth not desire to be made manifest.

canonical_statement: Manifestation is synonymous with the process of becoming and is therefore transient.

attributions.surface_quote: All that is made manifest is subject to becoming.

canonical_statement: The unmanifest divine principle is the causal agent that brings all other things into manifestation through the act of thought.

attributions.surface_quote: He thinketh all things manifest.

canonical_statement: The act of creation is identical to the act of thinking manifestation into existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Thinking-manifest is nothing else than making.

canonical_statement: The Divine manifests through all things, particularly those it wills to manifest.

attributions.surface_quote: He manifests through all things and in all.

canonical_statement: The Unmanifest can only be perceived by the faculty of thought, which is itself unmanifest.

attributions.surface_quote: Thought alone sees the Unmanifest, in that it is itself unmanifest.

canonical_statement: The existence of cosmic order, measure, and boundaries necessitates a governing intelligence or Maker.

attributions.surface_quote: It could not be that number, place and measure could be kept without someone.

canonical_statement: The Divine is present within the individual; failure to perceive the inner self precludes perception of the Divine.

attributions.surface_quote: If what is within thee even is unmanifest to thee, how shall He be manifest?

canonical_statement: The cosmos is characterized by the coexistence of motion and stillness, both governed by a single divine sway.

attributions.surface_quote: To see all these beneath one sway - the motionless in motion.

canonical_statement: The existence of the cosmos necessitates a singular, intelligent creator.

attributions.surface_quote: doth such workmanship as this exist without a Worker?

canonical_statement: The essence of the Divine is the continuous act of creation.

attributions.surface_quote: it is impossible that anything should be, so ever is He not unless He ever makes

canonical_statement: The Divine is the totality of existence, encompassing both manifest and unmanifest states.

attributions.surface_quote: He is Himself, both things that are and things that are not.

canonical_statement: The Divine is immanent in all things, rendering the distinction between creator and creation illusory.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou art whatever I may be; Thou art whatever I may do

canonical_statement: The Divine transcends all categories, names, and temporal limitations.

attributions.surface_quote: He is the God beyond all name; He the unmanifest

canonical_statement: The Divine encompasses the totality of existence and non-existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou art all that which doth exist, and Thou art what doth not exist

canonical_statement: The structure of reality is a hierarchical progression from matter to soul, mind, and finally God.

attributions.surface_quote: subtler part of matter is the air, of air the soul, of soul the mind, and of mind God

canonical_statement: The Divine essence is identical to the Good, existing eternally as a static, self-sufficient, and immutable source.

attributions.surface_quote: Good is God Himself eternally... essence, from every kind of motion and becoming free.

canonical_statement: The Divine is exempt from all passions, needs, and external influences, as these are properties of the realm of becoming.

attributions.surface_quote: He stands not in need of any thing... nor is there aught superior to Him.

canonical_statement: The Good cannot exist within the realm of genesis or becoming, as all generated things are subject to passion and change.

attributions.surface_quote: Wherefore in genesis the Good can never be, but only be in the ingenerate.

canonical_statement: The Cosmos is only partially good insofar as it acts as a creator, but it remains fundamentally flawed due to its passible and mutable nature.

attributions.surface_quote: In this way is the Cosmos Good; that, in so far as it doth make all things.

canonical_statement: In the human realm, 'good' is merely a relative term representing the absence or minimization of 'bad', rather than an absolute state.

attributions.surface_quote: In man by greater or less of bad is good determined.

canonical_statement: The absolute nature of goodness is exclusively inherent to the divine essence.

attributions.surface_quote: In God Alone Is Good And Elsewhere Nowhere

canonical_statement: The material world is inherently devoid of the Good, which exists only in the divine essence.

attributions.surface_quote: the name alone of Good is found in men, the thing itself nowhere

canonical_statement: Material bodies are incapable of containing the Good due to their entanglement with suffering and error.

attributions.surface_quote: no material body doth contain It

canonical_statement: The essence of God is identical to the Beautiful and the Good.

attributions.surface_quote: God's essence is the Beautiful; the Beautiful is further also Good.

canonical_statement: Visible objects are merely images or representations, whereas the true realities are invisible to the physical eye.

attributions.surface_quote: all the things that fall beneath the eye are image-things

canonical_statement: The Good and the Beautiful are inseparable from God and cannot exist within the realm of living creatures.

attributions.surface_quote: they cannot be joined with aught of other things that live

canonical_statement: The path to the divine is achieved exclusively through the synthesis of devotion and gnosis.

attributions.surface_quote: One is the Path that leadeth unto It - Devotion joined with Gnosis.

canonical_statement: Ignorance of the divine is the fundamental cause of human suffering and spiritual entrapment.

attributions.surface_quote: The ill of ignorance doth pour o'er all the earth and overwhelm the soul.

canonical_statement: The physical body acts as a restrictive container or 'cloak' that obscures the soul's perception of truth.

attributions.surface_quote: The soul that's battened down within the body, preventing it from fetching port.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is non-sensory and can only be apprehended through the mind and heart.

attributions.surface_quote: No ear can hear Him, nor can eye see Him, but only mind and heart.

canonical_statement: Sensory experience is a deceptive mechanism that binds the soul to material corruption.

attributions.surface_quote: The web of ignorance... the living death, sensation's corpse.

canonical_statement: The fundamental nature of existence is eternal; what is perceived as death is merely a transformation of form.

attributions.surface_quote: No one of existing things doth perish, but men in error speak of their changes.

canonical_statement: The Cosmos is an immortal, living entity, and therefore no constituent part of it can undergo true destruction.

attributions.surface_quote: Cosmos is second God, a life that cannot die; no part of this should die.

canonical_statement: The Creator is the eternal, unbegotten source, while the Cosmos is a secondary, sustained, and immortal manifestation of that source.

attributions.surface_quote: First is God the universals' Maker. Second is he after His image, Cosmos.

canonical_statement: The Eternal exists as a self-caused, non-contingent reality, while the Cosmos derives its immortality from the Father.

attributions.surface_quote: The Father is Himself eternal of Himself, but Cosmos hath become eternal by the Father.

canonical_statement: Matter is inherently chaotic and requires the imposition of a spherical, divine structure to maintain form.

attributions.surface_quote: Matter, when it was yet incorporate, was in unorder.

canonical_statement: Death is not the loss of the body, but the dissolution of its composition back into a state of unorder.

attributions.surface_quote: Dissolution restores them to those bodies which can never be dissolved.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness is uniquely structured to perceive both the physical Cosmos and the bodiless, divine Mind.

attributions.surface_quote: Man hath conception of the first; for of the one 'tis sensible as of a body.

canonical_statement: The hierarchy of existence is nested: the Cosmos exists within God, and Man exists within the Cosmos.

attributions.surface_quote: Understand the Cosmos is by God and in God; but Man by Cosmos and in Cosmos.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness is defined by the integration of sense and thought, whereas non-human life forms integrate sense primarily with nature.

attributions.surface_quote: In other lives sense is at-oned with Nature, but in men thought.

canonical_statement: Sense and thought are fundamentally unified in the human experience despite their distinct functional orientations toward matter and substance.

attributions.surface_quote: Unto me both seem to be at-one and not to differ - in men I mean.

canonical_statement: Mind and thought are distinct entities, analogous to the relationship between God and divinity.

attributions.surface_quote: Mind doth differ just as much from thought as God doth from divinity.

canonical_statement: Human cognition requires the integration of both sense and thought.

attributions.surface_quote: Neither without sensing can one think, nor without thinking sense.

canonical_statement: Human thought is determined by the source of its inspiration, either divine or demonic.

attributions.surface_quote: Mind conceives good thoughts from God, contraries from daimonials.

canonical_statement: The material world is the designated domain for evil, while the Cosmos remains distinct from it.

attributions.surface_quote: Bad must needs dwell on earth, where 'tis in its own place.

canonical_statement: The enlightened individual possesses the capacity to transform perceived evil into good through Gnosis.

attributions.surface_quote: He alone who maketh bad things good.

canonical_statement: The Cosmos possesses a unique, unified form of sense and thought distinct from human cognition.

attributions.surface_quote: Cosmos possesseth sense-and-thought peculiar to itself.

canonical_statement: The Cosmos functions as a cyclical mechanism that manifests, dissolves, and renews all life forms as an instrument of the Divine Will.

attributions.surface_quote: The Cosmos makes all things, and makes them back into itself again.

canonical_statement: The Cosmos is simultaneously the container of life and the creator of life.

attributions.surface_quote: It is at the same time the Place of Life and its Creator.

canonical_statement: The diversity of material bodies is determined by the speed of the movement of the Cosmos.

attributions.surface_quote: It is the speed of Cosmos' Course that works the manifoldness of the kinds of births.

canonical_statement: God is not separate from the universe; rather, God is the totality of all things that exist.

attributions.surface_quote: He is them all Himself. He doth not get them from without, but gives them out.

canonical_statement: Understanding is epistemologically equivalent to belief; lack of understanding is equivalent to disbelief.

attributions.surface_quote: To understand is to believe, to not believe is not to understand.

canonical_statement: The human mind possesses an inherent capacity to transcend discursive reason and attain direct apprehension of truth.

attributions.surface_quote: mighty is the mind... it hath the power to come before [thee] to the truth

canonical_statement: The capacity to comprehend metaphysical truth is contingent upon a prior state of understanding or divine aid.

attributions.surface_quote: unto those who understand them not, incredible

canonical_statement: The essence of the Divine is defined as the active will for all things to exist.

attributions.surface_quote: God's energy is then His Will; further His essence is to will the being of all things.

canonical_statement: The Divine is the fundamental subsistence of all things, distinct from the process of creation.

attributions.surface_quote: God is the to be of all that are not yet; subsistence self of everything.

canonical_statement: The Divine is not a 'maker' subject to temporal fluctuation, but a constant cause of being.

attributions.surface_quote: I will not say makes; the maker is defective for long periods.

canonical_statement: The fundamental nature of the Good is that it is inherently knowable.

attributions.surface_quote: The distinctive feature of the Good is that it should be known.

canonical_statement: All existence is contingent upon the Divine will, which precedes and enables all becoming.

attributions.surface_quote: Apart from the Good's will, nor being nor becoming could e'er be.

canonical_statement: The vision of the Divine Good enhances rather than blinds the perceiver's capacity for sight.

attributions.surface_quote: it shineth forth and maketh to increase the seeing of the eye

canonical_statement: True gnosis of the Divine is achieved only through the cessation of sensory activity and verbal thought.

attributions.surface_quote: Gnosis of the Good is holy silence and a giving holiday to every sense.

canonical_statement: The soul can be transformed into divine essence while still embodied through the contemplation of the Good.

attributions.surface_quote: it is possible that a man's soul should be made like to God

canonical_statement: Individual souls are fragmented portions of a singular All-soul that animates the cosmos.

attributions.surface_quote: from one Soul - the All-soul - come all these souls

canonical_statement: Souls undergo a process of evolutionary transmigration across different biological forms based on their moral state.

attributions.surface_quote: souls that live in air change to men, while human souls reach the first step of deathlessness

canonical_statement: The soul's ultimate potential is to ascend through the hierarchy of existence to join the choir of the Inerrant Gods.

attributions.surface_quote: they circle to the choir of the Inerrant Gods

canonical_statement: Moral failure in a human incarnation results in the regression of the soul into lower biological forms.

attributions.surface_quote: if a soul on entering the body of a man persisteth in its vice... it turns into the path that leads to creeping things

canonical_statement: Ignorance of the nature of reality and the Good constitutes the fundamental vice of the soul.

attributions.surface_quote: the soul's vice is ignorance

canonical_statement: Gnosis is a distinct faculty from sensory perception, representing the culmination of divine science.

attributions.surface_quote: Gnosis is far different from sense

canonical_statement: The material universe is structured through the interaction of antithetical and contrary forces.

attributions.surface_quote: all things must consist out of antithesis and contrariety

canonical_statement: The cosmos is a material entity in a state of perpetual becoming, lacking the perfection of the Good.

attributions.surface_quote: Cosmos is beautiful, but is not good

canonical_statement: Mortality is determined by the ratio of soul to body; greater proximity to the intelligible 'head' grants immortality.

attributions.surface_quote: things which have a greater share of body than of soul are subject unto death

canonical_statement: The universe is a unified life composed of both hylic (material) and intelligible components.

attributions.surface_quote: the universe consists of both the hylic and of the intelligible

canonical_statement: The Cosmos is characterized by motion but is immortal, whereas man is characterized by both motion and mortality.

attributions.surface_quote: Cosmos also is not good in that it suffers motion... man... subject to death.

canonical_statement: The human constitution is a hierarchical vehicle consisting of mind, reason, soul, spirit, and body.

attributions.surface_quote: mind in the reason, the reason in the soul, soul in the spirit, and spirit in the body.

canonical_statement: All existence originates from a single, unmoved Source, which is the One.

attributions.surface_quote: from one Source all things depend; while Source dependeth from the One and Only.

canonical_statement: Salvation is achieved through the acquisition of divine knowledge (Gnosis) of God.

attributions.surface_quote: This is the sole salvation for a man - God's Gnosis.

canonical_statement: The soul's descent into the physical body causes forgetfulness of the divine, which manifests as vice.

attributions.surface_quote: body grows in bulk and draweth down the soul... then doth the soul cut off itself.

attributions.surface_quote: mind, stripped of its wrappings... taking unto itself a fiery body, doth traverse every space.

attributions.surface_quote: It taketh, then, the soul for as it were an envelope.

canonical_statement: The mind's natural state is fire, which is incompatible with the density of an earthly body.

attributions.surface_quote: mind... hath for its body fire. For earth doth not bear fire.

canonical_statement: A pious soul, upon liberation from the body, transforms into pure mind.

attributions.surface_quote: such a soul becomes entirely mind.

attributions.surface_quote: impious soul remains in its own essence, chastised by its own self.

attributions.surface_quote: no other body can contain a human soul... not... changed into a beast.

attributions.surface_quote: mind becomes a daimon... scourgeth it with whips made of its sins.

attributions.surface_quote: to a better state the soul doth pass; it cannot to a worse.

attributions.surface_quote: The higher, further, have in charge the lower; the gods look after men.

attributions.surface_quote: dispensation of the universe, depending from the nature of the One, pervading all things through the Mind.

canonical_statement: The soul is functionally dependent on the Mind; without it, the soul lacks the capacity for reason, perception, and true humanity.

attributions.surface_quote: soul without the mind can neither speak nor act.

attributions.surface_quote: man is a thing-of-life divine; man is not measured with the rest of lives.

canonical_statement: Humanity and divinity possess an ontological equivalence in power and potential.

attributions.surface_quote: the gods and men are very whit in power each with the other equal.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness possesses the capacity to transcend physical spatial limitations while remaining embodied.

attributions.surface_quote: without e'en quitting earth, he doth ascend above.

canonical_statement: Humanity is defined as a mortal god, while divinity is defined as an immortal human.

attributions.surface_quote: man on earth is god subject to death, while god in heaven is man from death immune.

canonical_statement: The totality of existence is governed by the interaction of the Cosmos and Man, both originating from a singular source.

attributions.surface_quote: the dispensation of all things is brought about by means of there, the twain − Cosmos and Man − but by the One.

attributions.surface_quote: God maketh Aeon; Aeon, Cosmos; Cosmos, Time; and Time, Becoming.

attributions.surface_quote: Cosmos will never be destroyed, for Aeon's indestructible.

attributions.surface_quote: God in Mind; and Mind, in Soul; and Soul, in Matter.

attributions.surface_quote: all this Body... is full of Soul; and Soul is full of Mind, and Mind of God.

attributions.surface_quote: naught is like to That which hath no like, and is Alone and One.

attributions.surface_quote: Mind Unto Hermes

attributions.surface_quote: No one of these could be apart from God.

attributions.surface_quote: Working by Himself, He ever is at work, Himself being what He doth.

attributions.surface_quote: Death is not the destruction of those that are at-oned, but the dissolving of their union.

attributions.surface_quote: Bid thy soul go unto any land... not as if passing from place to place.

attributions.surface_quote: Think thyself deathless and able to know all.

attributions.surface_quote: Think that thou art at the same time in every place

attributions.surface_quote: The Mind, O Tat, is of God's very essence.

attributions.surface_quote: In irrational lives, Mind is their nature.

attributions.surface_quote: In lives irrational He doth co-operate with each one's nature; but in the souls of men He counteracteth them.

attributions.surface_quote: the Soul likewise of itself drawing near her Maker, is the Cause of Life

canonical_statement: The totality of existence is unified under a single soul, life, and material substrate.

attributions.surface_quote: For there is one Soul, one Life and one Matter.

canonical_statement: The divine is a singular entity that manifests its activity through the multiplicity of the world.

attributions.surface_quote: He therefore being One, doth all things in many things.

canonical_statement: Individual sensory and cognitive functions are unified by a single underlying agent.

attributions.surface_quote: It is not one that seeth... but One that doth all these things.

canonical_statement: The essence of the divine is defined by perpetual, necessary creative activity; inactivity would imply imperfection.

attributions.surface_quote: If there be any thing which he doth not do, then is he... imperfect.

canonical_statement: All temporal events—past, present, and future—are the necessary and continuous work of the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: It is the necessary work of God that all things should be made.

canonical_statement: The concepts of Life, Beauty, Goodness, and God are ontologically identical.

attributions.surface_quote: And this is life. And this is the Fair. And this is the Good. And this is God.

canonical_statement: The Creator is immanent within the creation, acting as the sole agent of all activity.

attributions.surface_quote: being himself the only Workman he is always in the Work

canonical_statement: All existence is sustained by a singular, divine life force; separation from this source results in non-existence.

attributions.surface_quote: if they were separated from him, must needs fall and die

canonical_statement: Life is defined as the functional union of Mind and Soul.

attributions.surface_quote: Life is the union of the Mind and the Soul.

canonical_statement: Death is not the annihilation of components, but the dissolution of the union between Mind and Soul.

attributions.surface_quote: death is not the destruction... but a dissolving of the Union.

canonical_statement: The world undergoes constant transformation and occultation, but is never fundamentally destroyed.

attributions.surface_quote: the World is changed... but that it is never dissolved.

canonical_statement: The divine essence possesses an incorporeal, singular Idea that manifests all forms through physical bodies.

attributions.surface_quote: He hath therefore one Idea... which shews all forms by the Bodies.

canonical_statement: The essential nature of the divine is the continuous act of creating and sustaining life.

attributions.surface_quote: the Life and Motion of God, to move all things, and quicken them.

canonical_statement: God does not exist within a spatial container, as space is a property of static bodies.

attributions.surface_quote: All things are in God, not as lying in a place

canonical_statement: The incorporeal is characterized by infinite capacity, speed, and power, transcending physical limitations.

attributions.surface_quote: nothing is more capacious, than that which is incorporeal, nothing more swift, nothing more powerful

canonical_statement: The human soul possesses the capacity for instantaneous presence across all locations, independent of physical movement.

attributions.surface_quote: Not as passing from place to place, but suddenly it will be there.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is understood only by the human mind when it equates itself with the divine through the expansion of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: If therefore thou wilt not equal thy self to God, thou canst not understand God.

canonical_statement: Cognition of the divine requires the subject to transcend the limitations of time and physical embodiment.

attributions.surface_quote: transcending all Time, become Eternity and thou shalt understand God

canonical_statement: The soul is capable of simultaneous awareness of all temporal states, including birth, death, and the afterlife.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou shalt at once understand thy self, not yet begotten... to be dead, the things after death

canonical_statement: Identification with the physical body and its limitations constitutes the primary obstacle to divine knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: if thou shut up thy Soul in the Body... what hast thou to do with God

canonical_statement: All phenomena in the universe are manifestations or images of the Divine.

attributions.surface_quote: there is nothing which is not the Image of God.

canonical_statement: The Divine is inherently visible through the totality of created things.

attributions.surface_quote: God is invisible, but be advised, for who is more manifest than He.

canonical_statement: The human Mind is ontologically identical to the essence of God.

attributions.surface_quote: The Mind, O Tat, is of the very Essence of God.

canonical_statement: The Mind is not a separate entity from God but is unified with the Divine essence.

attributions.surface_quote: The Mind therefore is not cut off, or divided from the essentiality of God.

canonical_statement: The presence of Mind is a universal property of all living souls, though its function varies by species.

attributions.surface_quote: For where there is a Soul, there is the Mind.

canonical_statement: The soul becomes susceptible to negative states when it descends into and identifies with the physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: the Soul being in the Body, is straightway made Evil by Sorrow, and Grief.

canonical_statement: The Mind acts as a corrective force that opposes the natural inclinations of the human soul to restore its proper state.

attributions.surface_quote: in men it worketh against their Natures.

canonical_statement: The Mind functions as a corrective governor of the Soul, preventing it from descending into irrationality and brutishness.

attributions.surface_quote: the Mind resisting it procureth Good to the Soul, as a Physician health to the Body.

canonical_statement: Atheism is the primary pathology of the Soul, as it disconnects the Soul from the governing influence of the Mind.

attributions.surface_quote: the great Disease of the Soul is Atheism

canonical_statement: All physical actions and events are governed by the necessity of Fate.

attributions.surface_quote: All things, O Son, are the work of Fate

canonical_statement: The experience of suffering is a necessary consequence of committing evil acts within the framework of Fate.

attributions.surface_quote: it is decreed by Fate, that he that doth any evil, should also suffer for it.

canonical_statement: While all humans are subject to Fate, those governed by the Mind are not subject to the same internal viciousness as the irrational.

attributions.surface_quote: rational men... do not suffer like unto other men, but being free from viciousness

canonical_statement: The rational individual experiences the consequences of their actions as the agent of those actions.

attributions.surface_quote: The rational man will not suffer for Adultery, but as the Adulterer.

canonical_statement: While physical change and generation are inescapable, the individual possessing Mind can transcend moral vice.

attributions.surface_quote: It is impossible to escape the Quality of Change, but the Viciousness, he may escape.

canonical_statement: All intelligible entities are fundamentally unified as a single essence.

attributions.surface_quote: All Things are one thing, Especially Intelligible Bodies.

canonical_statement: Human existence is defined by participation in Power, Act, and Eternity.

attributions.surface_quote: We live in Power, in Act and in Eternity.

canonical_statement: The human soul, being of divine origin, possesses the capacity to transcend the constraints of Fate.

attributions.surface_quote: The Soul that is of God, can do whatsoever it will.

canonical_statement: Incorporeal entities residing within a physical body are subject to passion and motion.

attributions.surface_quote: All incorporeal things that are in the Body, are possible, nay, they are properly Passions.

canonical_statement: Liberation from the physical body results in liberation from passion.

attributions.surface_quote: Being freed from the Body, it is freed likewise from Passion.

canonical_statement: The individual mind is a manifestation of a singular, universal consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Of the Common Mind to Tat.

canonical_statement: All entities, whether corporeal or incorporeal, are subject to the processes of action and passion.

attributions.surface_quote: there is nothing impassible, but all things are passible.

canonical_statement: Action and passion are ontologically identical, differing only in linguistic designation.

attributions.surface_quote: Action and Passion are the same thing.

canonical_statement: Humanity possesses Mind and Reason, which function as faculties equivalent to immortality.

attributions.surface_quote: God hath freely bestowed upon man... Mind and Speech... equal to immortality.

canonical_statement: The hierarchical structure of existence proceeds from God to Mind, to Soul, to Word, and finally to Body.

attributions.surface_quote: the Soul to be in the Body, the Mind, in the Soul, the Word... in the Mind, and the Mind in God.

canonical_statement: The universe is governed by the instruments of Necessity, Providence, and Nature.

attributions.surface_quote: Necessity, and Providence, and Nature, are the Organs or Instruments of the World.

canonical_statement: Intelligible entities possess an essence defined by absolute identity.

attributions.surface_quote: every one is but the Essence of them in Identity.

canonical_statement: The identity of compound bodies is preserved through their constant transformation into other forms.

attributions.surface_quote: Bodies that are put together... make their changes into other, having this Identity.

canonical_statement: Numerical structure is the fundamental requirement for the existence, composition, and dissolution of all things.

attributions.surface_quote: Without number it is impossible there should be consistence or constitution.

canonical_statement: The underlying matter of the universe is singular and unified.

attributions.surface_quote: And the Matter is One.

canonical_statement: The universe is a living entity that contains no death, as death is incompatible with the nature of God.

attributions.surface_quote: There is nothing dead, that either hath been, or is, or shall be.

canonical_statement: Death is a misnomer for the dissolution of compound bodies, which serves the purpose of renewal rather than destruction.

attributions.surface_quote: They do not die, but as compound Bodies they are dissolved.

canonical_statement: Motion is the essential operation of life, and nothing in the universe is truly unmovable.

attributions.surface_quote: What is there in the World unmovable? Nothing at all.

canonical_statement: Motion is a necessary condition for the generation of any entity.

attributions.surface_quote: It is impossible that anything that bringeth forth should bring forth without motion.

canonical_statement: All entities within the world are subject to processes of augmentation or diminution.

attributions.surface_quote: Whatsoever is in the world is moved either according to augmentation or diminution.

canonical_statement: The totality of the world is unchangeable, while its constituent parts are subject to change.

attributions.surface_quote: The whole world is together, it is unchangeable, but all the parts thereof are changeable.

canonical_statement: Death is not the destruction of essence, but an occultation or hiding of that which was.

attributions.surface_quote: Change is not death, but an occultation or hiding of that which was.

canonical_statement: All fundamental components of existence—matter, life, spirit, soul, and mind—are inherently immortal.

attributions.surface_quote: All things are immortal, matter, life, spirit, soul, mind.

canonical_statement: Humanity possesses a unique capacity to receive and converse with the Divine.

attributions.surface_quote: Man, who both receiveth God, and converseth with him.

canonical_statement: God is omnipresent, existing both around and through all things as both Act and Power.

attributions.surface_quote: God is both about all things, and through all things, for he is both Act and Power.

canonical_statement: All phenomena, including matter, body, and essence, are manifestations of divine activity.

attributions.surface_quote: Whether thou speak of Matter, or Body, or Essence, know that all these are acts of God.

canonical_statement: God is omnipresent and constitutes the entirety of existence; there is no place where God is not.

attributions.surface_quote: And there is not any thing of all that hath been, and all that is, where God is not.

canonical_statement: The divine nature transcends spatial and temporal categories such as greatness, place, quality, figure, or time.

attributions.surface_quote: About God, there is neither Greatness, Place, Quality, Figure, or Time.

canonical_statement: The universe was brought into existence through the divine Word rather than physical labor.

attributions.surface_quote: The Workman made this Universal World, not with his Hands, but his Word.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is omnipresent, eternal, and the singular creative agent of the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: present everywhere, and being always, and making all things

canonical_statement: The divine body is non-material and transcends physical dimensions and elemental properties.

attributions.surface_quote: not tangible, nor visible, nor measurable, nor extensible

canonical_statement: All physical elements originate from the divine essence, which is synonymous with the Good.

attributions.surface_quote: neither Fire, nor Water, nor Air, nor Wind, but all these things are of him

canonical_statement: Human beings possess a dual nature consisting of both an immortal and a mortal component.

attributions.surface_quote: he sent Man an Immortal and a Mortal wight

canonical_statement: Humanity is distinguished from other living beings by the possession of speech and mind.

attributions.surface_quote: Man had more than all living Creatures... because of his Speech, and Mind

canonical_statement: The Mind is a divine gift distributed selectively as a reward for spiritual striving.

attributions.surface_quote: it pleased him to set that in the middle among all souls as a reward

canonical_statement: Humanity is divided into those who possess Mind and those who possess only Speech and sensory perception.

attributions.surface_quote: he divided Speech among all men, but not Mind

canonical_statement: Possession of the Mind grants immortality and the capacity to comprehend all levels of reality.

attributions.surface_quote: partook of the gift of God, these... are rather immortal than mortal men

canonical_statement: Attachment to the physical body is fundamentally incompatible with the attainment of divine Mind.

attributions.surface_quote: Except thou first hate thy body, thou canst not love thy self

canonical_statement: The state of being mortal and the state of divine knowledge are mutually exclusive.

attributions.surface_quote: it is impossible to be conversant about things Mortal and Divine

canonical_statement: Human existence is defined by a binary choice between the corporeal and the divine, which are mutually exclusive.

attributions.surface_quote: For the things that are, being two Bodies, and things incorporeal... no man can choose both.

canonical_statement: Human beings are the originators of evil through their preference for the corporeal over the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: God is innocent or guiltless, but we are the causes of Evil, preferring them before the Good.

canonical_statement: The ultimate divine reality is infinite, formless, and lacks a beginning, existing solely of itself.

attributions.surface_quote: For the Good is not to be transcended, it is unbounded and infinite; unto itself without beginning.

canonical_statement: Human knowledge of the divine does not constitute the beginning of the divine, but merely the beginning of human awareness.

attributions.surface_quote: Our knowledge is not the beginning of it, but shews us the beginning of its being known.

canonical_statement: The incorporeal divine cannot be manifested or perceived through the medium of a physical body.

attributions.surface_quote: It is impossible, that any thing incorporeal, should be made known, or appear to a Body.

canonical_statement: The First Principle of all existence is self-caused and does not derive from any prior cause.

attributions.surface_quote: Nothing is without a beginning, but the Beginning is of nothing, but of itself.

canonical_statement: The ultimate principle of reality is an indivisible, self-originating Unity that generates all multiplicity without itself being subject to division or increase.

attributions.surface_quote: Unity therefore being the Beginning, containeth every number, but itself is contained of none.

canonical_statement: All created or begotten entities are inherently imperfect and subject to the processes of division, growth, and decay.

attributions.surface_quote: Every thing that is begotten is imperfect, and may be divided, increased, diminished.

canonical_statement: The perception of the divine image is an active, transformative process that exerts a magnetic pull upon the observer's consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Them that can see, and behold it, it holds fast and draws unto it.

canonical_statement: Sense and Understanding are fundamentally united in human beings.

attributions.surface_quote: unto me, they appear to be both one, or united

canonical_statement: The Mind stands in relation to Understanding as God stands to Divinity.

attributions.surface_quote: the Mind differs from Understanding, as much as God from Divinity

canonical_statement: Understanding and the Word (Speech) are mutually dependent instruments of manifestation.

attributions.surface_quote: neither is the Word pronounced without Understanding, neither is Understanding manifested without the Word

canonical_statement: Understanding can operate independently of sensory input, as evidenced by dream states.

attributions.surface_quote: it is possible that the Understanding may understand without Sense

canonical_statement: Human understanding is actualized when the sensory faculties of the body and soul are in accord.

attributions.surface_quote: when both parts of the Sense accord one with another, then is the understanding childed

canonical_statement: The human mind acts as a receptive vessel for external influences, manifesting either divine or demonic seeds into active operations.

attributions.surface_quote: The Mind brings forth all Intellections or Understandings. Good ones when it receiveth good Seed.

canonical_statement: Knowledge of God functions as a transformative state that renders all worldly experiences inherently good to the knower.

attributions.surface_quote: The Godly man laying hold on Knowledge... to him all things are good.

canonical_statement: Human identity is bifurcated into material and essential types, determined by the source of their understanding.

attributions.surface_quote: Every man doth not enjoy Understanding; for one man is material, another essential.

canonical_statement: The physical world possesses a singular, unified consciousness that serves as the instrument for the divine will.

attributions.surface_quote: The World hath a peculiar Sense and Understanding... the Organ or Instrument of the Will of God.

canonical_statement: The motion of the world acts as a mechanism for generating, infecting, and purifying qualities within existence.

attributions.surface_quote: The Motion of the World stirring up Generations, makes Qualities, infecting some with evilness, and purifying some with good.

canonical_statement: Sense perception and intellectual understanding are distinct faculties of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Of Sense and Understanding.

canonical_statement: The world functions as a divine instrument that perpetually receives, dissolves, and renews all living seeds.

attributions.surface_quote: receiving all Seeds into itself from God... it maketh all things effectually and dissolving them, reneweth

canonical_statement: The world is simultaneously the location of life and the active agent of its manifestation.

attributions.surface_quote: it is at once, both the Place and the Workman of Life.

canonical_statement: Physical bodies are composed of varying combinations of the four elements, determining their weight and complexity.

attributions.surface_quote: Bodies are from the Matter... some are of the Earth, some of Water, some of Air

canonical_statement: God is the ultimate source of the world, and the world is the source of all things within it.

attributions.surface_quote: God is the Father of the World, but the World is the Father of things

canonical_statement: Individual sense and understanding are not intrinsic to living things but are inspired from the surrounding environment.

attributions.surface_quote: Sense and the Understanding, cometh into them from without, inspired by that which compasseth them

canonical_statement: God is not separate from existence; rather, God is the totality of all things, manifesting them outwardly.

attributions.surface_quote: He is All Things, not receiving them from without, but exhibiting them outwardly.

canonical_statement: The essence of God is the eternal, unceasing movement of all things.

attributions.surface_quote: the Sense and Understanding of God, to move all things always.

canonical_statement: Understanding is a prerequisite for belief in metaphysical truth.

attributions.surface_quote: For to understand, is to believe, but not to believe, is not to understand.

canonical_statement: Language serves as a limited vehicle to guide the mind toward transcendent truth.

attributions.surface_quote: my speech or words reach not unto the Truth, but the Mind is great, and being led... by Speech, is able to attain to the Truth.

canonical_statement: The capacity for science and art is contingent upon the possession of reason.

attributions.surface_quote: Science and Art were the Operations of the rational... unreasonable Creatures partake not of Science, or Art.

canonical_statement: Instinctual behaviors in non-human animals are expressions of Nature rather than learned science or art.

attributions.surface_quote: These things they do... not by Science or Art, but by Nature

canonical_statement: Operations are unbodily entities that require physical bodies to manifest their effects.

attributions.surface_quote: Operations... being unbodily, are in Bodies, and work by Bodies.

canonical_statement: Because operations are unbodily, they are inherently immortal.

attributions.surface_quote: in as much as they are unbodily, thou must needs say they are immortal.

canonical_statement: Unbodily operations are perpetually bound to physical manifestation because they cannot function independently.

attributions.surface_quote: in as much as they cannot act without Bodies, I say, they are always in a Body.

canonical_statement: Entities subject to Providence or Necessity are compelled to perform their proper operations continuously.

attributions.surface_quote: cannot possibly remain idle of their own proper Operation.

canonical_statement: The essence of existence is eternal, as the union of body and life is constant.

attributions.surface_quote: that which is, shall ever be; for both the Body, and the Life of it

canonical_statement: Acts and operations are immortal and require a corporeal substrate to manifest.

attributions.surface_quote: Acts or Operations are immortal... Acts or Operations cannot be without Bodies.

canonical_statement: The soul can exist independently of a mortal body, but acts and operations cannot.

attributions.surface_quote: the Soul is not always in a Mortal Body, for it can be without a Body

canonical_statement: A body cannot exist or function without the presence of a soul.

attributions.surface_quote: the Body cannot Consist without a Soul.

canonical_statement: The active principle (the agent) is superior to and governs the passive principle (the patient).

attributions.surface_quote: everything that acteth or operateth is stronger, and ruleth; but that which is actuated

canonical_statement: Acts and operations govern both animate and inanimate matter.

attributions.surface_quote: Acts or Operations do not only actuate... living... Bodies, but also breathless Bodies

canonical_statement: All existence is defined by constant activity and operation, which are inherently immortal.

attributions.surface_quote: Let therefore every act or operation be understood to be always immortal.

canonical_statement: The world is a self-sustaining system that continuously generates phenomena to prevent corruption.

attributions.surface_quote: The World is never widowed... in labour to bring forth the things that are.

canonical_statement: Sensory perception is a corporeal phenomenon that is dependent on the physical body and ceases upon its death.

attributions.surface_quote: Senses are both corporeal and mortal, having so much existence as the Body.

canonical_statement: Eternal entities lack sensory perception because they are not subject to the influx or departure of external stimuli.

attributions.surface_quote: To Eternal Bodies there is nothing comes, nothing departs; therefore there is no sense.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness possesses unique operations distinct from bodily functions, expressed through intellect, arts, and sciences.

attributions.surface_quote: Other Operations are proper to the Souls of Men, by Arts, Sciences, Studies, and Actions.

canonical_statement: All entities, including inanimate objects, possess operations and sensory capacities.

attributions.surface_quote: In every Body... even in things inanimate.

canonical_statement: Sensory experience is categorized by the nature of the entity: rational, irrational, or inanimate.

attributions.surface_quote: Senses of things rational, are with Reason; of things unreasonable, Corporeal only.

canonical_statement: Pleasure and grief are essential mechanisms for perception in living beings.

attributions.surface_quote: Without these, it is impossible that a living wight... should perceive.

canonical_statement: Sensory perception is a bodily phenomenon, distinct from the incorporeal soul.

attributions.surface_quote: Sense is neither Operation, nor Soul... it must needs be a Body.

canonical_statement: Absolute truth is inaccessible to humans due to their composite, imperfect nature.

attributions.surface_quote: It is not possible that man being an imperfect wight... should speak with any confidence.

canonical_statement: Truth resides exclusively within eternal, incorporeal entities.

attributions.surface_quote: Truth is only in the Eternal Bodies.

canonical_statement: Physical bodies are composite structures of elemental forces that lack inherent ontological truth.

attributions.surface_quote: our Bodies consist of all these... yet there is neither Fire, nor Earth... true.

canonical_statement: Earthly phenomena are merely imitations or images of Truth, rather than Truth itself.

attributions.surface_quote: All things therefore upon Earth... are not Truth, but imitations of the Truth.

canonical_statement: Human perception is inherently deceptive unless influenced by a divine operation from above.

attributions.surface_quote: when the fantasy hath an influence from above, then it is an imitation of Truth.

canonical_statement: Truth is ontologically distinct from matter and cannot exist within the physical realm.

attributions.surface_quote: Truth indeed is nowhere at all upon Earth... for it cannot be generated.

canonical_statement: Truth is defined as an unchangeable, incorporeal, and perfect Good.

attributions.surface_quote: Truth is the most perfect Virtue... not troubled by Matter, not encompassed by a Body.

canonical_statement: Truth is defined as that which is immutable, self-constituted, and eternal.

attributions.surface_quote: the true to be that which abides the same, and is Eternal

canonical_statement: All things subject to change, generation, or corruption are inherently false or illusory.

attributions.surface_quote: Everything that is begotten or made, and changed is not true

canonical_statement: Human identity is not true because it is composed of multiple, shifting forms and appearances.

attributions.surface_quote: man consists of many things and doth not abide of himself

canonical_statement: The First Truth is non-material, incorporeal, immutable, and exists independently of shape or color.

attributions.surface_quote: The One and Only... not of Matter, that is not in a body

canonical_statement: Generation and physical existence are dependent upon the process of corruption.

attributions.surface_quote: without corruption, there can no Generation consist

canonical_statement: The cycle of generation and corruption is necessary to prevent the cessation of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Corruption followeth every Generation, that it may again be generated.

canonical_statement: Entities subject to change and corruption lack ontological truth, existing only as appearances or fantasies.

attributions.surface_quote: things that are generated of Corruption are false... we must call these things fantasies.

canonical_statement: Falsehood and the appearance of things are derivative operations originating from the absolute Truth.

attributions.surface_quote: Falsehood is the Work of Truth.

canonical_statement: The soul is inherently immortal, while the body is a construct subject to processes of constitution and dissolution.

attributions.surface_quote: the Soul is Immortal, and what operation that is, which constitutes the Body, and dissolves it.

canonical_statement: Death is a linguistic construct or misnomer, as true destruction does not exist.

attributions.surface_quote: Death is a conception of a name... there is nothing in the whole world destroyed.

canonical_statement: The universe is an immortal living entity, and its constituent parts cannot perish.

attributions.surface_quote: it is impossible that any part of an Immortal living Wight should die.

canonical_statement: God is the eternal, unmade creator, while the world is a secondary, immortal image of God.

attributions.surface_quote: The first of all is God... The second is the World, made by him.

canonical_statement: There is a categorical distinction between that which is eternal and that which is ever-living.

attributions.surface_quote: that which is ever living, differs from that which is eternal.

canonical_statement: The Eternal is self-caused and exists as the totality of the Universe.

attributions.surface_quote: The Eternal was not begotten... it is always made. The Eternal is the Universe.

canonical_statement: Matter is inherently disordered until structured by the Father into a spherical, immortal body.

attributions.surface_quote: Matter was incorporeal... disordered... the Father made it all into a Body.

canonical_statement: Death is not the destruction of substance, but a dissolution of form and a privation of sense.

attributions.surface_quote: There is made a privation of Sense, but not a destruction of Bodies.

canonical_statement: Humanity is created in the image of the World, possessing a Mind that allows for the apprehension of both the corporeal and the incorporeal.

attributions.surface_quote: Man, made after the Image of the World; and having... a Mind.

canonical_statement: The World exists within God, and Man exists within the World, with God as the ultimate origin and end.

attributions.surface_quote: The World is of God and in God; but Man of the World.

canonical_statement: The nature of reality is composed of individual entities that can be understood through systematic contemplation.

attributions.surface_quote: learn the Nature of the things that are

canonical_statement: All phenomena are created by an external agent rather than self-originating.

attributions.surface_quote: Those things that are made, are not made by themselves, but by another.

canonical_statement: The creator is uncreated and ontologically prior to all created things.

attributions.surface_quote: he unmade, and more ancient than the things that are made.

canonical_statement: The creator manifests the invisible into the visible through continuous creation.

attributions.surface_quote: the things that are made, are visible, but he is invisible; and for this cause, he maketh them

canonical_statement: Reality is a binary system consisting exclusively of the Maker and the Made.

attributions.surface_quote: there is nothing in the middle, between these Two, nor is there any third.

canonical_statement: The divine nature is characterized by the triad of Power, Operation, and Goodness.

attributions.surface_quote: God because of his Power; the Maker because of his Working; the Father, because of his Goodness.

canonical_statement: The Creator and the created are ontologically identical and inseparable.

attributions.surface_quote: neither is it possible that the maker should be without the thing made

canonical_statement: The totality of created things constitutes the body of the Divine.

attributions.surface_quote: this making, or facture is as it were the Body of God

canonical_statement: Evil and imperfection are not inherent to the Divine but are byproducts of the process of generation.

attributions.surface_quote: vicissitude of Generation doth make them, as it were to blossom out

canonical_statement: Change serves as a necessary purgative process within the cycle of generation.

attributions.surface_quote: make Change to be, as one should say, The Purgation of Generation

canonical_statement: God is defined as the essence of Good, which is synonymous with the power to create all things.

attributions.surface_quote: Good is all power, to do or make all things

canonical_statement: The totality of existence is comprised of two fundamental principles: the Divine and the process of generation.

attributions.surface_quote: they are all but four, God and Generation, in which are all things.

canonical_statement: The Divine acts as the source of immortality, while the material realm is defined by change and motion.

attributions.surface_quote: God in Heaven sow Immortality, in the Earth Change in the whole Life, and Motion.

canonical_statement: The structure of the universe is observable through the analogy of agricultural cultivation.

attributions.surface_quote: Look upon the Husbandman... So doth God in Heaven sow Immortality
